## Introduction

This report examines how caterpillar abundance varies across habitat types,
using a Poisson generalised linear model and a boxplot of counts by habitat.
It produces the numeric results in the "Caterpillar Abundance" section of the
manuscript and Figure 1.

### Packages

The analysis uses three packages: `dplyr` (summarising and filtering data),
`ggplot2` (Figure 1) and `here` (relative file paths). They are loaded with
`library()` at the start, so the packages needed are listed in one place and a
missing package gives an error straight away. Functions from these packages are
also called with their package name (for example `dplyr::filter()`), so it is
clear where each one comes from. The R and package versions used are listed under
[Session information](#session-information) at the end of this report.

```{r packages}
## Load packages (R 4.1 or later is needed for the |> pipe)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
```

## Data

### Import

Caterpillar counts and their associated habitat are read in from a CSV file,
using `here::here()` so the path is relative to the project folder and does not
rely on local file paths.

```{r import}
## Load caterpillar abundance data (relative path, no local file paths)
data <- read.csv(here::here("caterpillar_data", "data.csv"))
```

### Removing erroneous records

Values from habitat D are removed, as these are known to be an error.

```{r filter}
## Remove values from habitat D as these are an error
filtered_data <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(habitat != "D")
```

### Descriptive summary

The mean number of caterpillars, with standard deviation, is summarised for
each habitat, after habitat D has been removed.

```{r summary}
## Summarise the mean number of caterpillars, with standard deviation, by habitat
summary_data <- filtered_data |>
  dplyr::group_by(habitat) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_count = mean(caterpillar_count),
    sd = sd(caterpillar_count)
  )

summary_data
```

## Statistical analysis

A Poisson generalised linear model is used to analyse caterpillar abundance
by habitat.

```{r model}
## Run a Poisson generalised linear model to analyse caterpillar abundance
## varying with habitat. Produces numeric results in "Caterpillar Abundance"
model1 <- glm(caterpillar_count ~ habitat,
              family = poisson, data = filtered_data)

summary(model1)
```

Habitat significantly alters caterpillar abundance.

## Visualisation

```{r figure1}
## Create Figure 1, caterpillar count against habitat
figure1 <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  filtered_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = habitat, y = caterpillar_count)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot() +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()

print(figure1)
```

Habitat E has the highest caterpillar count.
